status_at_registration: prospective; no quality execution has occurred
scope: Authored development/regression diagnosis. Cases were designed after inspecting existing v0.11 weaknesses; this is not an independent holdout, external-product score or latency experiment.

metrics.answerable: Count the expected first session and complete original evidence separately; aggregate separately by mode/budget/limit.
metrics.conflict: Both equally timed recorded declarations are evidence. Report their coverage separately; one-result requests cannot contain two separate pages. Do not label a chosen timestamp or ranking as resolved authority.
metrics.missing: Count whether related context is returned. Nonempty context is not generated-answer accuracy or failure to abstain; the API is an evidence retriever.
metrics.empty_scope: An absent exact project ID must return no results and cannot fall back to another book.
metrics.relevance_control: Retain full responses; compare results, context and candidate_count with the baseline. Relevance-mode current-evidence counts are controls, not current-state accuracy claims.
metrics.integrity: Every result must pass exact original-page follow-up, source-slice and excerpt-coordinate checks, exact context framing, project scope, result limit and character budget. Independently recompute every saved score and the closed request matrix.

source_binding: Require requested worktree HEAD, complete tracked runtime bytes and actual imported package/store/backend. Bind the loaded native extension and evaluator closure before and after execution. Save every response and journal attempted requests before each call.
comparison_rules: Do not change the old 80-question fixture, questions, labels, common packer, historical reports or external ranking settings.
Do not remove a difficult case or change its gold after observing results. Any protocol correction requires a new version and retains the original attempt.
Keep every failed setup/execution and use a fresh output path for retries.
First-session or source-span regressions must be disclosed per case, even if aggregate results improve.
Supplementary expected-session checks do not prove universal decision authority or truth. Complex Chinese prose, dotted identifiers and equal-time conflicts intentionally expose limits.
Crowding cases contain repeated authored text; repetition count is not a count of independent quality questions.

External engines may be compared only in a separately registered supplied-page protocol with actual package execution and unchanged common packing. Native excerpts cannot substitute for those external scores.
No new latency ranking or universal-superiority claim is accepted from these executions.
